summary: This paper, written by ROS Navigation maintainers, surveys state-of-the-art mobile robot navigation algorithms in ROS 2 and Nav2, organized by fundamental problems. The portion present covers global path planners (holonomic NavFn, Lazy Theta*-P, 2D-A*, and kinematically feasible Hybrid-A* and State Lattice) with a benchmark table, and begins local trajectory planners (reactive DWA/DWB controllers), with the note cut off mid-sentence. It also introduces Nav2 as a successor to the ROS 1 Navigation Stack and summarizes the ecosystem's rapid development.
one_line: Survey by ROS Navigation maintainers reviewing global and local path planning algorithms in ROS 2 Nav2, with benchmarks.
key_facts: The survey paper is authored by Steve Macenski (ROS 2 Project Lead, Samsung Research), Tom Moore, David V. Lu, Alexey Merzlyakov, and Michael Ferguson.
Nav2 was built to leverage innovations in behavior trees and maintains production-grade quality with 90% unit test coverage.
The original Navigation Stack was developed at Willow Garage for the PR2 robot and was based around an unconfigurable state machine, move base.
Nav2 global planning methods are Navigation Function, 2D-A*, Theta*, Hybrid-A*, and State Lattice planners.
Global path planners are all extensions of Dijkstra's algorithm aiming to find the path with minimal cost.
The benchmark used a AMD Ryzen 5 5600X CPU with Ubuntu 20.04, 1,000 randomly generated start and goal poses through a 20% randomly occupied 10,000m2 map, with start and goal at least 3 meters apart.

In the benchmark, NavFn planned in 61.02 ms with a path length of 52.25 m, Lazy Theta*-P in 94.42 ms with 50.28 m, Smac 2D-A* in 88.82 ms with 49.65 m, Smac Hybrid-A* in 38.77 ms with 50.78 m, and Smac State Lattice in 39.40 ms with 50.51 m.
NavFn is the default planning algorithm in Nav2 and is the oldest algorithm in Nav2, derived from the ROS 1 Navigation Stack.
Lazy Theta*-P uses a Moore neighborhood and L2 distance heuristic and evaluates line-of-sight on the current node's grandparent rather than parent.
Hybrid-A* was proposed by Stanford during the DARPA Urban Challenge as an extension of traditional grid-A*.
State Lattice was utilized by Carnegie Mellon University in the DARPA Urban Challenge and uses offline computed motion primitives.
Nav2 includes trajectory planners Dynamic Window Approach (DWA), Regulated Pure Pursuit (RPP), Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI), and Rotation Shim controllers.
DWB is currently the default local trajectory planner in Nav2, a refactor of the Base Local Planner and DWA Local Planner from ROS 1.
The survey notes that DWB's numerous, highly interrelated parameters make tuning complex, and poorly tuned configurations can create extremely suboptimal behaviors.
